== Team winners (2026-10-16) ==
=== Possibly faulty data ===
* 2025 DRTORCH interview auto-captions (BillBisco2, 29 May 2025): Feldman said he was the only American on a team of four, named something like "three Europeans an American", and recalled "Martin Logan", "Bastion", and a fourth he could not remember. The wiki had treated those as [[Maarten Logghe]] and [[Bastian Winkelhaus]].
* Best-supported list is the Trandosite Akesson interview of 31 August 2000: Akesson, Paul Feldman, Koen Meijsen, Yannick LaPointe. Koen Meijsen is [[Koen Meijssen]]; Yannick LaPointe is [[Yannick Lapointe]]. Feldman's March 2000 Torch Industries pages confirm he was on the winning team and do not name teammates.

== Team photo search (26 October 2026) ==
=== Build notes ===
* Team photo: Decipher's Sunday album photo sun24 shows Akesson, Meijssen and Lapointe; the caption says Feldman is missing. Only the 50×38 index thumbnail (<code>photos/SUN/small/sun24.gif</code>, Wayback 31 May 2000) survives. The full-size <code>photos/SUN/large/sun24.jpg</code> returns 404 on every Wayback host (decipher.com, www, www1), so I uploaded the thumbnail as [[:File:DecipherCon 1999 Team Event winners sun24.gif]].
* Feldman photo: sun07 ("feet first") was already on the wiki as [[:File:Paul Todd Feldman DecipherCon 1999.jpg]], so I reused it rather than upload a second copy.
* Searched with nothing more found: Lalumiere's wrap-ups (Thursday to Saturday; no Sunday wrap-up was archived), the Trandosite Akesson interview (an Akesson portrait only), and ''Star Wars Insider'' 48 (the World Championship feature shows Worlds finalists, not the team event).
=== Missing data ===
* A larger copy of sun24. [[Kevin Reitzel]]'s public Facebook album "Decipher Days 1996-2006" (<code>facebook.com/media/set/?vanity=kevin.reitzel&set=a.10230980334389335</code>) is not readable without a browser session, so it has not been checked. == Team name and roster source (2026-10-26) ==
* Team name and roster history come from [[Martin Akesson]]'s DeckTech report ([https://web.archive.org/web/20261025134508/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-01-09-world-championships-by-martin-akessond163/ Preserved copy]): the team was "non americans +1". Bastian Winkelhaus and then Martin Falke were named before Feldman joined. The sun24 caption gives the same name as "Non-Americans + 1".
* Correction to the build notes above: a Sunday (Day 4) Lalumiere wrap-up was archived, at <code>lalumiere/index.html</code> (Wayback 22 January 2000). It does not mention the team event.
* The Photographs section now uses a large packed gallery of each winner's Decipher photo. The sun24 thumbnail is shown on its own above it.
